pairs.subject: agent-instruction-files
pairs.evidence: lib/claudeCli.ts:279 The reasoning door's argv (-p, --output-format, --model, --effort, --allowed-tools "", --max-turns 1) has no --safe-mode, and its spawn at lib/claudeCli.ts:383 passes no cwd. So every frames, research and recalibrate turn (lib/turns/runner.ts -> reason -> runClaude) starts in the server's own directory, the repo root, and is briefed by the developer CLAUDE.md, which was written about a different job. The writer and reviewer seams in the same context, and the sibling claudeCliRetrieve door, all close that path with --safe-mode.

techniques.evidence: lib/claudeCli.ts:279 Product reasoning turns inherit the repo's developer instruction file because the argv has no --safe-mode and the process runs from the repo root. The agentic seam gets this right: --safe-mode at lib/agent/agentArgs.ts:37, an os.tmpdir() workspace at lib/articles/agentSteps.ts:36, and assertIsolatedWorkspace at lib/agent/agentArgs.ts:91.

lib/agent/cliSeam.ts:13 The tool set, file scope and config loading are enforced through CLI flags and a pre-spawn workspace check rather than prose in the prompt. Where agy has no flag that can enforce read-only, the code says so and isolates the run (reviewerEngines.ts:47).
lib/agent/reviewerCommand.ts:22 No skill set is compiled for several hosts. The per-engine reviewer argv suppresses the reviewers' own rule loading, but that is not skill compilation.

pairs.registryProposal: workspace-ancestry-isolation could name a third case beside upward inheritance and downward injection: a product that shells out to a coding-agent CLI as a reasoning engine from its own repo root. That turn is briefed by the developer instruction file on every product call, and the fix is a config-suppression flag on that spawn, not a workspace move.
